transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for calling S-Net technical support, my name is Laura. How can I help you today?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Hi Laura. I'm calling because we pay for the S-Net Smart Wi-Fi Guarantee, but we have a complete dead zone in our newly converted loft bedroom. We get zero signal up there, and your guarantee says reliable Wi-Fi in every room or money back.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I understand your concern about not getting Wi-Fi coverage in your loft conversion, Ava. Let me look at your broadband profile and discuss your options.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Thank you Laura, because my husband is trying to work from the loft and he can't connect to video calls at all.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Before we review your Wi-Fi guarantee terms, Ava, could you please verify your installation address and your four-digit account security PIN?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, it is 78 St Albans Road, Watford, WD17 1SJ, and the security PIN is 4920.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for verifying those details, Ava. I have your Gigafast 500 broadband package open on my system.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Great, thanks.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: So just to confirm what you are experiencing: you have subscribed to our Smart Wi-Fi package, but you are experiencing a complete dead spot in your top-floor loft conversion where your husband is unable to work or connect to the internet. Is that correct?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, exactly. Downstairs near the Hub we get five hundred megabits, on the first floor we get about two hundred, but the moment you walk up the stairs into the loft, it drops to zero bars.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: When you have a loft conversion, builders typically install foil-backed Celotex or Kingspan insulation boards across the roof rafters and floor timbers.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, it has modern insulation throughout the attic space.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Foil-backed insulation acts as a Faraday shield that completely blocks radio frequency signals, so our Wi-Fi guarantee generally doesn't cover structural shielding like that.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Wait a minute! When I signed up for the Smart Wi-Fi Guarantee, the sales rep specifically told me it guarantees at least thirty megabits in every single habitable room in the house, including loft conversions!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I understand why you feel that way, Ava, but foil insulation is a physical building material that radio waves physically cannot penetrate. You would be much better off going to Currys and buying a third-party Powerline adapter kit.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Why should I spend eighty pounds at Currys when I am paying eight pounds a month to S-Net specifically for your Wi-Fi guarantee and mesh booster pods?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Because even if we sent you an S-Net Wi-Fi Pod, if the wireless signal cannot penetrate the foil floor, the pod will not receive a signal to repeat.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Your contract terms state that if a Wi-Fi Pod doesn't achieve thirty megabits, you send an engineer out to install an Ethernet backhaul or fit an extra pod, and if that fails, you give a one hundred pound bill credit!

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Let me check what equipment is currently logged on your account.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: We only have the main Hub 5 router on the ground floor right now.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Have you run the S-Net Connect app Wi-Fi home scan from inside the loft bedroom?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Yes, I ran the home scan yesterday while standing at the loft desk, and the app flashed red saying Signal Unacceptable: Zero Megabits.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Looking at your telemetry logs... yes, the app logged a signal level of minus eighty-nine dBm on the 5GHz radio in the loft.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Minus eighty-nine dBm means no usable connection, right?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes, anything below minus eighty dBm results in packet drop and connection termination.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: So that formally triggers the Smart Wi-Fi Guarantee process.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Under standard procedure, we would dispatch one S-Net Wi-Fi Pod in the post for you to plug into the first-floor landing.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: We tried placing our laptop on the first-floor landing and the signal was only two bars. If the landing signal is weak, putting a repeater there won't deliver thirty megabits up to the loft.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: That is why I advised that a Powerline kit running through the electrical wiring would be simpler for you than going through our engineering stages.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Laura, I want S-Net to honor the guarantee I pay for each month. Please follow your official guarantee procedure.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Very well, Ava. To follow the guarantee terms, I can arrange for an S-Net Home Tech Specialist engineer to visit your property.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Thank you. What will the Home Tech Specialist do during the visit?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The technician carries specialized RF spectrum analyzers, high-gain Wi-Fi Pods, and can run an internal data cable if wireless mesh cannot bridge the floor barrier.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Can they install a hardwired Ethernet cable up to the loft if the wireless mesh is blocked by the foil?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes, if the engineer determines that wireless propagation is physically blocked by foil insulation, they have authorization to install a surface-mounted Cat6 Ethernet cable up to the loft.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That would permanently solve the issue for my husband's desk.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: And if the engineer is unable to achieve a verified thirty megabits in that room after testing, the guarantee stipulates a one hundred pound account credit.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That's exactly what the terms said when we signed up.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Please bear with me while I place you on a brief hold for about two minutes while I check the technician booking calendar.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for your patience while holding, Ava. I have access to the Home Tech Specialist scheduling system.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Thank you Laura. What appointments are available?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I have an appointment slot available this Friday between one o'clock and six o'clock in the afternoon.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Friday afternoon works perfectly, my husband will be working downstairs so he can let the technician in.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: I will book that appointment slot under booking reference WIF-883019.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Is there any callout charge for this visit?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Because you subscribe to the Smart Wi-Fi Guarantee and the home scan verified an unacceptable dead spot, the engineer visit is free of charge.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That's great. Will the technician bring the Wi-Fi Pods with them?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Yes, the technician carries up to three Wi-Fi Pods in their van stock, along with Ethernet cabling and wall faceplates.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: And will they test the speed on my husband's work laptop before they leave?

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The engineer is required to run a certified speed audit from the dead spot location and upload the speed test certificate to your file before closing the job.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That ensures the thirty megabits threshold is actually verified.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Will your husband need the technician to configure a specific Wi-Fi band or separate SSID for work devices?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: No, our devices use band steering automatically on the S-Net Hub.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: The Wi-Fi Pods seamlessly integrate with your existing Hub SSID, so no device passwords need to be updated.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That makes setup very straightforward.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: You will receive an SMS reminder on Friday morning with the technician's name and a live tracking link when they are en route.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: That is very helpful so we know when to expect them.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Is there anything else regarding your Wi-Fi coverage or broadband settings that I can check today, Ava?

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: No, Laura, thank you for booking the specialist engineer for Friday. We look forward to having it resolved.

transcript.speaker: Agent
transcript.text: Thank you for choosing S-Net today, Ava. Have a wonderful rest of your day.

transcript.speaker: Customer
transcript.text: Thanks Laura, goodbye.
